heroHeadline: Simonyi Telescope Pauses for Engineering Downtime as Rubin Team Reports First Globular Cluster Find
heroSubtitle: The Simonyi Survey Telescope paused nightly science observations on Sep 14 for a previously scheduled operations engineering downtime — its first since the Legacy Survey began — with a Sep 18 summit report showing camera cooling, computing, and dome systems still mid-recovery and no return-to-sky date yet announced. Separately, a Rubin team led by Aashay Pai and William Cerny (Yale) posted a Sep 14 preprint describing Rubin-GC1, the survey's first globular cluster discovery: a faint, ~31-kiloparsec-distant Milky Way satellite in Ophiuchus likely accreted from the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy's tidal stream, pending peer review. The find follows last month's confirmed extragalactic first, the ultra-faint dwarf galaxy Aquarius IV, also drawn from Early Data Preview 2. Before the summer storm, the survey had logged over 11,000 new asteroids and ~380 trans-Neptunian objects; a second EDP2 data phase remains due Q4 2026.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
